function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or instruction that gives a person or entity the power to act on behalf of another party. In many contexts—especially in finance, law, and governance—a mandate defines the scope, limits, and conditions under which the authorized agent may operate. Key points: | Aspect | Typical meaning | |--------|-----------------| | **Legal/Contractual basis** | A written agreement (e.g., a power‑of‑attorney, proxy, or service contract) that specifies who can act and how. | | **Scope of authority** | Can range from broad (full control over assets or decisions) to narrow (specific tasks like signing a single document). | | **Status categories** | • **Active** – currently valid and enforceable.
• **Pending** – awaiting approval or activation.
• **Inactive** – expired, revoked, or otherwise not in force. | In practice, you might see mandates used for: - **Financial services** – a bank account holder authorizing a third party to manage investments. - **Corporate governance** – shareholders granting a board member the right to vote on their behalf. - **Government procurement** – a public body giving a contractor the authority to deliver goods or services under a contract. Understanding the status of a mandate (active, pending, inactive) helps determine whether it can be relied upon for decision‑making or execution of duties.
